label: first occurrence of u/g/b/p/w (t>=2) or <DEL>, in sequences starting with v/n/j/1/c/y/a/k
explanation: Fires almost only while the original tokens are being read (71% of mass) and at the <DEL> step (29%); essentially never during the copy phase, and never at t=0 or 1. In the original phase it is driven by the input token: u is by far the strongest (35% of mass, 8.6x lift, top activations all on u), then g, b, p, and more weakly w. It fires mostly on the first occurrence of that token (in_first=1 holds 96% of mass) and peaks at t=3-4. It is strongly gated by sequence context, especially the first token: sequences starting with v, n, j, 1 or c have about 4x lift, and y, a, k about 2x. The <DEL> activation also depends on first_tok. Gating by first token pushes precision up sharply (u at t=3-4 with first_tok in v/n/j/1/c: precision 0.81), but recall falls. The predicate covers about 80% of activation mass at low precision (~0.21): most steps matching the context and token never fire, so some extra dependence on the prefix is not captured. Magnitude is highest for u at t=3-4 in v/n/j-initial sequences, while <DEL> activations sit around 0.3-0.6 of max. Digits 0/3, q and repeated tokens almost never fire.
